# relgap cache

relgap keeps HTTP responses under $XDG\_CACHE\_HOME/relgap/http (config cache.dir,
env RELGAP\_CACHE\_DIR). Each entry holds the response body and a few response headers (content
type, ETag, Last-Modified, Link); request headers and tokens are never stored.

An entry is fresh for a time that depends on the age of the newest release it describes:
1 hour under 7 days, 1 day under 6 months, 10 days when older. Answers from endoflife.date,
OSV, the CISA KEV catalog, EPSS, the Terraform registry, Artifact Hub, npm and PyPI stay fresh
for 1 day, and a 404 for 1 hour. cache.ttl\_override sets a fixed TTL per source
(github, endoflife, osv, kev, epss) or host. A stale GET is revalidated with If-None-Match, and an
authenticated 304 from GitHub doesn't count against the rate limit.

--offline answers from the cache only, --refresh revalidates everything, --no-cache skips it.

## Usage

```sh
relgap cache <command>
```

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Examples

```sh
relgap cache info
relgap cache prune --older-than 720h
relgap cache clear
```

## Subcommands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| [relgap cache clear](/cli/cache/clear) | Delete every cache entry |
| [relgap cache info](/cli/cache/info) | Show the cache directory, entry count, size and freshness |
| [relgap cache prune](/cli/cache/prune) | Delete entries not used for a while |
